text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] P1 — SRV lookup error spike for _backend._tcp.svc.cluster.local in us-east-1b. 45% error rate over 5m. Pager: @sara-oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/srv-dns-failures :rotating_light:

sara-oncall: ack, I'm on it. Paging @jamie-sre @mike-eng. Any deploys in the last hour?

mike-eng: no deploys from our side. Looking at k8s metrics — coredns pods in us-east-1b showing repeated 5xx on SRV queries. From one coredns pod: `dig +short SRV _backend._tcp.svc.cluster.local @127.0.0.1` -> timeouts and truncated responses.

jamie-sre: taking lead. Quick hypothesis: consul/etcd leader flapping across AZ causing inconsistent SRV answers. Consul metrics show increased election latency and multiple leader changes in the last 10m. Logs: `agent: failed to contact server` from two consul servers in us-east-1b.

katie-cse: customer impact — CS reports two high-value customers (acme-inc, deltaapp) saw 502s for chat search and background jobs. They're escalated; ETA for first customer update 10m.

sara-oncall: mitigation plan (quick): 1) prefer consul servers in us-east-1a from coredns forwarders in us-east-1b; 2) add short-term static fallback entries for critical services; 3) track consul leader stability. I'll coordinate changes.

jamie-sre: patching coredns configmap to add forwarders to healthy consul nodes in us-east-1a and increase UDP timeout. Applying now. Example snippet I'm using:

```
# kubectl -n kube-system edit configmap coredns
# inside consul plugin block:
consul {
  forward . 10.2.10.4 10.2.11.7
  upstream_timeout 5s
  health_check 3s
}
```

sara-oncall: before the config change, let's scale coredns in us-east-1b to reduce pressure: `kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment coredns --replicas=6 --selector=topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-east-1b` (will do rolling increase).

mike-eng: scaled coredns (2 -> 6) in us-east-1b. Seeing one pod CrashLoopBackOff — logs show repeated `consul: connection refused` and `context deadline exceeded` when contacting consul IPs.

deploy-bot: deploy coredns-config-update (deploy/12345) started by jamie-sre at 1795551401.

jamie-sre: config applied and rollout restart initiated: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment coredns` — restarting pods now.

katie-cse: CS update sent: "We're investigating SRV resolution errors affecting some requests in us-east. Mitigation in progress. Next update in 15m." :email:

mike-eng: digging into infra — found NLB health checks for consul servers in us-east-1b were failing (port 8300) due to a security group rule inadvertently blocking cross-AZ health probes. That explains intermittent unreachability.

jamie-sre: after coredns restart and NLB SG fix, SRV error rate dropped to ~8% and leader elections reduced. Running `consul operator raft list-peers` — shows stable leader in us-east-1a and healthy followers.

incident-bot: Severity downgraded to P2 at 1795551500.

sara-oncall: summary / handoff: 1) root cause: intermittent NLB/SG blocking health probes causing consul server flaps in us-east-1b -> inconsistent SRV responses. 2) short-term mitigations applied: patched coredns forwarders to prefer healthy consul nodes, scaled coredns in AZ, fixed NLB SG. 3) next actions: audit NLB health checks across regions, include failover routing in runbook, follow up postmortem. Handing off to @olivia-oncall for night shift at 03:00 UTC — leaving notes in runbook.

olivia-oncall: ack I have the handoff. I'll monitor SRV error rate, consul leader stability, and revert the temporary coredns forwards in 2 hours if stable. If errors spike, I'll escalate to @netops.

netops: noted — we'll audit NLB health checks and SG rules across affected AZs. Will follow up on final postmortem action items.

katie-cse: final customer update sent with timeline and mitigations. We'll include the follow-up postmortem and notify once complete.

sara-oncall: final check: SRV error baseline now 0.6%, no new customer reports, closing incident thread. :white_check_mark: (1795551600)
